formattedAddress: 11568, Taiwan, Taipei City, Nangang District, Sanzhong Village, Jingmao 2nd Rd, 131號1樓

text.text: My recent visit left me with mixed feelings compared to my previous experience, and overall it was not as good as the 101 store location, which I usually enjoy more. The atmosphere was still pleasant and the restaurant looked clean and well maintained, but the dining experience did not quite meet the expectations I had based on my first visit. The biggest issue was the waiting time for the food, which took a bit too long considering the restaurant was not overly busy at the time. When the dishes finally arrived, some of them were semi cold, which really took away from the overall enjoyment and made it feel as though the timing in the kitchen was not well coordinated. That said, the staff service was good though, and I want to give credit where it is due. The employees were polite, attentive, and made an effort to check in on us, which helped soften the disappointment slightly. Unfortunately, good service alone could not fully make up for the quality and temperature of the food on this visit. It was a bit disappointing as I had higher standard the first time I went, and I was hoping for the same level of consistency this time around. I still believe the place has potential, especially with such friendly staff, but there clearly needs to be better control over preparation time and food temperature. With some improvements in these areas, I think it could return to the level I experienced before and be much closer to what I expect from a restaurant of this type.

text.text:
Salt & Stone offers a comfortable environment with dedicated staff who are attentive and welcoming, which made the dining experience pleasant.

We started with the burrata salad, but the heavy acidity from the vinegar overpowered the dish, not one I’d recommend. The pizza with bacon, onion, and potatoes sounded promising, but the lack of seasoning and sweetness from the onion made it fall flat. Their signature roasted chicken was juicy and succulent, yet surprisingly lacking in flavor.

For dessert, the pecan pie could do without the whipped cream and cocoa powder, it distracts from what should be a simple, nutty finish.

Overall, while the service and atmosphere were lovely, the food didn’t quite live up to expectations.
